payload.name: Spatial asymmetry in VR menu visual search
payload.fact: Visual search in VR menu interfaces exhibits systematic spatial asymmetries, with the upper-right quadrant demonstrating the fastest response times and reduced gaze-based search effort.
payload.boundary: Simulated VR menu interfaces using screen-based eye-tracking.

provenance.title: Eye-Tracking-Based Evaluation of Visual Search Efficiency in Simulated VR Menu Interfaces: Effects of Card Layout Structure and Target Spatial Quadrant
provenance.quote_or_locus: Behavioral and eye-tracking analyses also revealed systematic spatial asymmetries, with the upper-right quadrant showing the fastest responses and reduced gaze-based search effort
